sulfurCube.title: Sulfur cube launch mechanics
sulfurCube.scope: Java Edition 26.2 mechanics · selected cube properties · primary player melee · cube initially at rest on a selected uniform flat floor
sulfurCube.assumptions.title: Scope and fixed assumptions
sulfurCube.assumptions.intro: This view keeps the following assumptions fixed:
sulfurCube.assumptions.call: A primary player melee hit always produces the ordinary E = 1 call when accepted. Sprinting or Knockback can produce one additional E = K/4 call; the calls are evaluated separately and in source order.
sulfurCube.assumptions.cube: The adult sulfur cube starts at rest and uses its JE 26.2 dimensions and the selected properties. The default state places its feet at (0, 0, 0).
sulfurCube.assumptions.aim: The aim point constructs the attacker's look direction; it is not a sampled collision point.
sulfurCube.assumptions.trajectory: The trajectory begins with the first cube movement update after the impulse and models repeated collision and rebound over the selected infinite, level, uniform floor. It includes source-ordered cutoff, friction, restitution, speed factor, gravity, air drag, and relevant floor callbacks. It excludes floor edges, gaps, walls, fluids, later attacks, honey side sliding, changing frosted ice, active explosive fuses, and other obstacles.
sulfurCube.invalidInputs: Enter valid cube properties, attack settings, and finite scene inputs; use a whole-number trajectory length from 0 to 1000 ticks, choose a supported uniform floor, and keep the aim point distinct from the eye position.
sulfurCube.controls.title: Inputs
sulfurCube.floor.ice_0_98: Ice / packed ice / static frosted ice
sulfurCube.properties.title: Archetype
sulfurCube.properties.archetypeDefinitio: An archetype is a Java Edition 26.2 property definition applied when the sulfur cube swallows a matching block item. It determines launch power, resistance, air drag, and other behavior.
sulfurCube.properties.absorbedBlockHelp: Search the 334 block items accepted by the vanilla Java Edition 26.2 sulfur cube.
sulfurCube.properties.blockResultsKeyboa: Use the arrow keys to move through the blocks, then press Enter or Space to select one.
sulfurCube.properties.blockNoResults: No absorbed blocks match this search and archetype filter.
sulfurCube.properties.archetypeHelp: Choose among the 12 vanilla Java Edition 26.2 sulfur-cube archetypes.
sulfurCube.properties.customHelp: Custom values persist when you leave Custom mode or change the selected block or archetype.
sulfurCube.properties.customInvalid: Enter finite values, keep knockback resistance from −2 to 1, bounciness from 0 to 1, and the air-drag and friction modifiers from 0 to 2048.
sulfurCube.properties.lockedHelp: These values are locked. Choose Custom to create a detached configuration.
sulfurCube.controls.damageArgumentHelp: The nonnegative damage value passed to knockback; this is not necessarily health lost.
sulfurCube.attack.title: Player melee attack
sulfurCube.attack.help: The full tool derives the damage passed to knockback and an ordered call sequence from these Java Edition 26.2 player-melee settings. The compact article view intentionally keeps its simpler one-call scope.
sulfurCube.attack.attackStrengthHelp: Attack cooldown recovery when the hit is processed.
sulfurCube.attack.survivalUnavailable: This combination is not obtainable in unmodified vanilla Survival: Knockback cannot be applied to a bare-hand attack.
sulfurCube.attack.trace.title: Ordered attack calls
sulfurCube.attack.trace.intro: Each call independently transforms and scales the launch power, clamps its components, and adds its velocity to the result of the preceding call.
sulfurCube.attack.trace.yaw: Player yaw used by extra call
sulfurCube.controls.coordinatesHelp: Use these fields as an alternative to the scene handles or to edit lateral X/Z coordinates outside the radial view.
sulfurCube.controls.cubeFeetHelp: World coordinates of the bottom center of the sulfur cube.
sulfurCube.controls.attackerFeetHelp: World coordinates used for the cube-to-attacker elevation calculation and horizontal base direction.
sulfurCube.controls.attackerEyesHelp: World coordinates supplied independently from the feet position. The default uses the standing-player eye height of 1.62 blocks; editing these coordinates is a diagnostic override of that relationship.
sulfurCube.controls.aimPointHelp: Defines look direction from the eye position. It does not represent where the attack collided with the cube.
sulfurCube.controls.uniformFloorHelp: Models an infinite level surface of the selected type, with its JE 26.2 collision height, friction, restitution, speed factor, bounce suppression, and relevant top-surface callback. It does not simulate finite terrain or arbitrary block layouts.
sulfurCube.controls.trajectoryTicksHelp: The maximum number of movement ticks to show, from 0 to 1000. While Default is active, the value follows deterministic settlement, subject to the 1000-tick safety cap. If the cap is reached first, the endpoint is marked as truncated and the trajectory may continue. Entering a value or clicking Default again turns Default off.
sulfurCube.scene.title: Radial vertical scene
sulfurCube.scene.subtitle: How aim and height angle determine launch velocity.
sulfurCube.scene.svgDescription: A pannable and zoomable radial side view showing the sulfur cube, the standing player's hitbox, feet and eyes, a fixed-length look arrow, launch velocity, and repeated trajectory arcs over a selected uniform floor.
sulfurCube.scene.reachMissWarning: Aim misses the cube within the 3-block melee reach.
sulfurCube.scene.reachInsideWarning: The cube cannot be targeted while the player's eyes are inside its hitbox.
sulfurCube.scene.aimHandleAria: Move aim point, currently x {x}, y {y}, z {z}. Arrow keys move by 0.25 blocks; hold Shift for 0.05-block steps.
sulfurCube.scene.attackerHandleAria: Move the attacker while preserving eye height and look direction. Arrow keys move by 0.25 blocks; hold Shift for 0.05-block steps.
sulfurCube.scene.cubeHandleAria: Move the sulfur cube by its center handle. Arrow keys move by 0.25 blocks; hold Shift for 0.05-block steps.
sulfurCube.scene.openPointsAfter: let you drag the sulfur cube, as well as the player and their aim.
sulfurCube.scene.compactHelp: On a computer, use the smaller scene to compare the effects of the aim and player height angle on the launch direction.
sulfurCube.scene.projectionHelp: The mechanics and numeric results use full 3D X/Y/Z geometry. This rendering projects them onto a vertical side-view plane whose horizontal axis stays fixed while objects move, so lateral X/Z changes may not be visually separable. Resetting the scene rebuilds that plane from the default feet positions.
sulfurCube.scene.trajectoryContinues: The trajectory has not settled after {ticks} ticks; the marked endpoint is the selected horizon, and motion continues.
sulfurCube.scene.trajectorySettledEarly: The cube settles after {shown} ticks, before the requested {requested}-tick horizon.
sulfurCube.topDown.title: Top-down horizontal scene
sulfurCube.topDown.subtitle: How full X/Z aim transforms the initial knockback direction into horizontal launch motion.
sulfurCube.topDown.help: The target bearing points from the player toward the cube and combines with the player's aim to define the horizontal aim error Δ. The initial knockback direction is then rotated by 1.6 × Δ; the final velocity and trajectory show the resulting horizontal motion. This scene displays the same full 3D mechanics evaluation as the radial view without recalculating it.
sulfurCube.topDown.svgTitle: Interactive top-down sulfur cube launch scene
sulfurCube.topDown.svgDescription: A pannable and zoomable top-down X/Z view showing the player, sulfur cube, aim, target bearing, initial and aim-adjusted knockback directions, final velocity, and trajectory.
sulfurCube.topDown.callRotatedTitle: Knockback step {call}: direction after aim adjustment
sulfurCube.topDown.cubeHandleAria: Move the sulfur cube in the X/Z plane. Arrow keys move by 0.25 blocks; hold Shift for 0.05-block steps.
sulfurCube.topDown.attackerHandleAria: Move the attacker in the X/Z plane while preserving eye height and look direction. Arrow keys move by 0.25 blocks; hold Shift for 0.05-block steps.
sulfurCube.topDown.aimHandleAria: Move the aim point in the X/Z plane while preserving its height. Arrow keys move by 0.25 blocks; hold Shift for 0.05-block steps.
sulfurCube.topDown.interactionHelp: Drag the open points to change X/Z position and aim. Vertical coordinates stay unchanged; use the radial scene for height changes.
sulfurCube.power.title: Horizontal/vertical power space
sulfurCube.power.subtitle: How aim and height angle determine launch power.
sulfurCube.power.caveat: This diagram shows internal power components, not velocity. To produce the velocity vector, the game scales the power by damage and knockback resistance, clamps its horizontal and vertical components, applies the final output factors, and directs the horizontal result away from the attacker. The resulting vector is then added to the cube's existing velocity.
sulfurCube.power.svgDescription: A diagram showing the selected base power, vertical aim transfer, feet-elevation rotation, and component-ratio cap inside the horizontal and vertical power axes.
sulfurCube.power.stages.aimHelpBefore: Vertical aim redistributes power between the two components using
sulfurCube.power.stages.elevationHelpBef: Relative attacker-feet elevation rotates the aim-adjusted vector by
sulfurCube.power.stages.cappedHelp: The height-adjusted vector is capped by the archetype values.
sulfurCube.power.sequenceExplanation: Starting from base power, aim currently applies a {percentage}% transfer ratio, so horizontal power is multiplied by {horizontalFactor} and vertical power by {verticalFactor}. Height then rotates this aim-adjusted vector by {degrees}°. Finally, {capDescription}
sulfurCube.power.sequenceCapApplied: the archetype cap multiplies the vector by {factor} to keep both components within its limits.
sulfurCube.power.sequenceCapNotApplied: the vector is already within the archetype limits, so the cap does not rescale it.

sulfurCube.readout.provenanceBehavior: Knockback and repeated uniform-floor motion are derived from locally decompiled Java Edition 26.2 code.
sulfurCube.readout.provenanceData: Resolved cube properties, dimensions, and uniform-floor profiles are derived from Java Edition 26.2 data and runtime initialization; Custom mode clearly separates reader-edited cube values.
sulfurCube.readout.standardMath: This version uses standard TypeScript number and trigonometric operations; source-precision emulation is planned separately.
